book_title: Chapter 3: The LDD Flywheel, Working Capital Plumbing & the FY2025 Dollar Waterfall
question: How does BrightSpring secure exclusive Limited Distribution Drug contracts, navigate PBM reimbursement and working-capital timing, and convert $12.9 billion of revenue into $395 million of Free Cash Flow?

epigraph.quote: Pharmacy gross profit per script rose 27% to $28.86, primarily driven by a favorable product mix.
epigraph.author: Jennifer Phipps, CFO, BrightSpring Health Services (Q3 2026 Earnings Call)

web_blocks.title: 3.1 The Limited Distribution Drug (LDD) Hub & Referral Network

web_blocks.html: Retail chain pharmacies compete on foot traffic and store convenience. Specialty pharmacy is won in biopharma boardrooms and oncology clinics instead [9]. When drugmakers launch complex orphan, oncology, or neurology drugs, they restrict supply to a small panel of accredited pharmacies [9]. These therapies are known as Limited Distribution Drugs (LDDs) [9]. Exclusive panels protect cold-chain handling, FDA REMS safety tracking, fast fill times, and patient-adherence data [9]. By Q2 2026, BrightSpring's portfolio had expanded to 155 LDDs across Onco360 and CareMed [4].

BrightSpring's distribution edge rests on two structural pillars. First, its centralized clinical hubs in Louisville, Kentucky pair 24/7 oncology-pharmacist counseling with prior-authorization and copay-assistance teams [9]. That support cuts prescription abandonment when patients face high out-of-pocket bills [9]. Second, its non-PBM-owned independent status appeals to community oncologists and drugmakers wary of CVS Caremark, OptumRx, or Express Scripts [9]. In Home & Community Pharmacy, PharMerica runs closed-door regional pharmacies linked to facility EHRs [3, 9]. Its couriers deliver blister packs and 24/7 stat emergency kits, while Provider Services pairs sterile infusion cleanrooms with ~30-state nursing branches [2, 8, 9].

web_blocks.title: 3.2 Reimbursement Mechanics, IRA Part D Headwinds & Working Capital Plumbing

web_blocks.html: Unit economics in specialty pharmacy depend on spread and service fees against Wholesaler Acquisition Cost (WAC), shaped by PBM contracts, wholesaler terms, and federal payor rules [1, 11]. Two structural concentrations sit behind those numbers (per the FY2025 Form 10-K and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 3) [1, 26]. First, government programs supply 68.2% of consolidated 9M 2026 revenue ($7,979.5 million of $11,700.1 million): Medicare Part D represents 29.7%, Medicare Advantage (Part C) 18.5%, Medicaid 11.4%, Medicare Part A 8.0%, and Part B 0.6%, leaving 28.8% commercial insurance and 3.0% private/other [26]. Under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), mandatory Medicare drug price negotiations, rebates, and Part D caps drove a $138.0 million (-7.9% YoY) nine-month revenue contraction in Home & Community Pharmacy (-$37.4 million in Q3 2026) [26, 33]. Second, on the supply side, PharMerica historically purchased pharmaceuticals via Walgreens' WBAD Membership Agreement and Joinder with AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation (ABDC / Cencora) ($147.8 million ABDC and $13.1 million WBAD invoice purchases disclosed under related-party terms in FY2025) before terminating WBAD in Q1 2025 and signing a standalone ABDC agreement on February 1, 2025 [1, 28].

Working capital acts as the main cash-flow governor—and a 2026 accounting shift changed its surface appearance [1, 26]. BrightSpring buys expensive specialty drugs upfront from wholesalers and ships scripts weeks before PBMs or government plans settle claims [1]. In FY2024, when the $120 million Silver settlement collided with inventory and receivable timing, Operating Cash Flow dropped to $23.8 million [1, 10]. By September 30, 2026, net accounts receivable reached $1,216.4 million (~26 days of Q3 annualized revenue), yet trade accounts payable stood slightly higher at $1,232.3 million [26]. Meanwhile, on-balance-sheet inventories dropped from $815.2 million at year-end 2025 to $671.6 million at September 30, 2026—not solely from faster turns, but because BrightSpring entered a $111.6 million off-balance-sheet supplier consignment arrangement in 2026 (zero at year-end 2025) where the supplier retains title and can demand return or redirection prior to dispensing [26]. That consignment structure freed $143.4 million of 9M 2026 cash flow from inventories, making BrightSpring's cash conversion sensitive to wholesaler payment and consignment terms [26].
Scaling FY2025 continuing operations to $100 of revenue separates pass-through drug billing from non-cash amortization and true free cash conversion [1].

web_blocks.caption: FY2025 Audited Continuing Operations Revenue-to-FCF Waterfall ($ Millions)
web_blocks.takeaway: Out of $12,910.6M of FY2025 continuing revenue, BrightSpring earned $1,517.8M gross profit (11.8%), $295.3M operating income (2.3%, or $2.29 per $100), and $104.8M net income (0.8%), while +$162.9M non-cash D&A add-back and +$222.5M working-capital bridge lifted CFO to $490.2M ($3.80 per $100) and Free Cash Flow to $394.7M [1].

web_blocks.title: The Thin-Margin, High-Cash-Conversion Reality
paragraphs: In FY2025, every $100 of BrightSpring revenue consumed $88.24 in drug and clinical service costs, leaving $11.76 in gross profit [1]. SG&A ex-D&A took $8.21, and D&A took $1.26, leaving $2.29 in GAAP operating profit [1]. Net interest took $1.22, and taxes took $0.26, leaving $0.81 in GAAP net income [1]. Non-cash amortization of $1.26 and low CapEx of $0.74 lifted Free Cash Flow to $3.06 per $100 of sales [1].

web_blocks.title: 3.4 Interest De-Escalation, Manufacturer Fees & Cash-Conversion Mechanics

web_blocks.html: Two unit-economic levers explain why BrightSpring's cash flow grows faster than top-line sales [1, 26]. First, specialty pharmacy earns both dispensing spread against WAC and contractual manufacturer service fees [9]. Drugmakers pay those fees for REMS safety tracking, adherence support, and clinical data reporting [9]. As Onco360 and CareMed scaled to 155 LDDs, pharmacy gross profit per script climbed steadily [3, 4, 27]. It rose from $17.83 in FY2024 to $21.64 in FY2025 (+21.4%) and $28.86 in Q3 2026 (+27% YoY) [3, 4, 27]. That trajectory backs CFO Jennifer Phipps's point that product mix drives unit profit [27].

Second, balance-sheet deleveraging directly boosts the bottom of the cash-flow waterfall [1, 26]. In FY2024, net interest of $190.5 million exceeded GAAP operating income of $112.3 million, creating a $(68.9) million GAAP net loss [1]. By FY2025, lower rates and debt paydown cut net interest 17.4% to $157.3 million against $295.3 million of operating income [1]. Then came the March 2026 Community Living sale ($811 million net pre-tax proceeds) and a $300 million First Lien paydown in Q2 2026 [4, 5, 26]. Lower interest expense frees asset-light operating cash flow ($204.3 million in Q3 2026 alone) to build free cash flow, while non-cash intangible amortization shields cash taxes [1, 26, 27].

book_paragraphs: To see why specialty pharmacy looks deceptive on a standard income statement, trace a single $100 bill through BrightSpring's FY2025 P&L. On the surface, the margins look razor-thin. Out of $12,911 million in continuing revenue, Cost of Goods Sold and Cost of Services took $11,393 million. That leaves $1,518 million in gross profit, or $11.76 per $100 of sales. When Onco360 dispenses a $15,000 cancer drug, BrightSpring books the full $15,000 as revenue and the ~$13,500 wholesale cost in COGS. The drugmaker sets the list price, and BrightSpring acts as the clinical tollbooth in the middle.

Follow that $11.76 of gross profit per $100 of revenue down the waterfall. SG&A—corporate overhead, prior-authorization hubs, pharmacist pay, and intangible amortization—consumed $1,223 million. That breaks into $1,060 million ex-D&A ($8.21 per $100) plus $163 million of D&A ($1.26 per $100). Operating income stood at $295 million, or a 2.3% margin ($2.29 per $100). Net interest took $157 million ($1.22 per $100), still over half of operating profit in 2025. Taxes took $33 million ($0.26 per $100), leaving $105 million in GAAP net income—less than one penny on the dollar.

Now look at the plot twist that draws cash-flow investors to this model. That $163 million of D&A is non-cash, mostly amortization of acquired intangibles from PharMerica and home-health deals. Meanwhile, BrightSpring spent only $95.5 million on CapEx, or 0.74% of sales. As a result, Operating Cash Flow reached $490.2 million and Free Cash Flow hit $394.7 million. That equals $3.06 of Free Cash Flow per $100 of sales, or 377% conversion of GAAP net income. As net interest drops from $190.5 million in FY2024 to $157.3 million in FY2025 and lower after Q2 2026's $300 million First Lien paydown, saved interest flows straight toward pre-tax cash flow.

CFO Jennifer Phipps summed up the unit-profit engine on the Q3 2026 call: 'Pharmacy gross profit per script rose 27% to $28.86, primarily driven by a favorable product mix.' On a routine generic pill at PharMerica, BrightSpring earns only a few dollars of gross profit. On a new Limited Distribution Drug at Onco360 or CareMed, it earns both dispensing spread against WAC and manufacturer service fees. Those fees cover REMS safety monitoring, cold-chain delivery, and patient adherence reporting. That is why gross profit per script rose from $17.83 in FY2024 to $21.64 in FY2025 and $28.86 in Q3 2026.

That cash-flow machine relies on tight working-capital plumbing—and a new 2026 consignment structure that deserves close inspection. BrightSpring ended Q3 2026 with $1,216.4 million in net accounts receivable (roughly 26 days of Q3 annualized revenue), offset by $1,232.3 million in trade accounts payable to drug wholesalers. Because payables exceed receivables, wholesaler credit terms effectively finance BrightSpring's specialty receivables float. Notice also why on-balance-sheet inventories fell from $815.2 million at year-end 2025 to $671.6 million at September 30, 2026 despite 25% top-line growth: Note 1 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reveals that BrightSpring entered a new supplier consignment arrangement in 2026 holding $111.6 million of off-balance-sheet inventory (versus zero at year-end 2025). While consignment liberated $143.4 million of 9M cash flow, the supplier retains title and can require return or redirection before dispensing—magnifying supplier dependence alongside PharMerica's standalone February 2025 contract with AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation (ABDC / Cencora) after exiting Walgreens' WBAD purchasing alliance.

You also have to watch how concentrated government payor rules hit the plumbing. Note 3 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q shows that 68.2% of BrightSpring's nine-month revenue comes from government programs: Medicare Part D (29.7%), Medicare Advantage Part C (18.5%), Medicaid (11.4%), Medicare Part A (8.0%), and Part B (0.6%). Under the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare Part D redesign and negotiated drug caps, Home and Community Pharmacy revenue declined $138.0 million (-7.9% YoY) across 9M 2026, including $37.4 million (-6.3%) in Q3 2026. Instead of chasing unprofitable nursing-home volume, management exited uneconomic LTC contracts and leaned harder into high-dollar oncology LDDs and home infusion.

Winning those 155 Limited Distribution Drug contracts is not luck. When a biotech spends a decade and a billion dollars launching a targeted lung-cancer pill, it cannot afford patient abandonment at a retail counter over a $2,500 copay or a slow prior authorization. Onco360 and CareMed run centralized clinical hubs in Louisville and nationwide to verify benefits, secure charity grants, track REMS rules, and provide 24/7 pharmacist triage. Independence from the Big Three PBMs makes BrightSpring a trusted, conflict-free partner for drugmakers—and keeps that $28.86 gross profit per script engine compounding.

That clinical hub also strengthens home infusion and regional LTC delivery. In Home and Community Pharmacy, PharMerica skips overnight parcel boxes in favor of closed-door regional pharmacies. Those sites link directly to nursing-home electronic health records, pack automated blister strips, and dispatch 24/7 stat couriers. In home infusion, BrightSpring's cleanrooms compound sterile IV therapies and coordinate with Adoration's 30-state nursing branches. A patient leaving the hospital receives both the compounded drug bag and the skilled nurse to start the IV line.

Step back from the FY2025 waterfall and the unit-economic lesson is clear. Do not be fooled by a 2.3% GAAP operating margin or a 0.8% GAAP net margin on pass-through drug sales. BrightSpring needs less than 0.8% of revenue for CapEx ($95.5 million in FY2025) and books $162.9 million in non-cash D&A. Every extra dollar of gross profit per script above fixed hub costs converts into free cash flow at a high rate. Watch three plumbing gauges: gross profit per script, Days Sales Outstanding on the $1.22 billion receivable balance, and falling quarterly interest expense.

book_callouts.title: Why 2.3% Operating Margin Isn't the Whole Story
book_callouts.text: Pass-through specialty drug costs make BrightSpring's percentage margins look like a grocery store (11.8% gross, 2.3% EBIT), but its asset-light CapEx (0.7% of sales) and non-cash intangible amortization convert 2.3% GAAP EBIT into 3.1% Free Cash Flow margin—and 377% net-income-to-FCF conversion in FY2025.
